idea.body: A solid's surface area is the total area of every face on the outside, found from its net, the shape it unfolds into flat. A prism's net is two matching ends plus rectangles for the sides. A cylinder's net is two circles plus one rectangle, since its curved side unrolls flat. A cone's net is one circle plus a curved wedge, whose area works out to pi times radius times slant height. A pyramid's net is one base plus a triangle for each side. A sphere has no flat net at all; its surface area is simply 4 times pi times its radius squared.

figure.alt: A cylinder, radius 5 and height 9 centimeters.

workedExample.prompt: A drone's cylindrical battery case has radius 3 centimeters and height 8 centimeters. Find its surface area, as a multiple of pi.
steps: Two circular ends contribute 2 times 3 squared, which is 18.
The curved side, unrolled flat, contributes 2 times 3 times 8, which is 48.
Add them: 18 + 48 = 66.
The surface area is 66 pi square centimeters.

figure.alt: A cylinder, radius 3 and height 8 centimeters.

ways.name: The net
ways.when: Use this any time you can unfold a solid into its flat pieces.
steps: A prism is 4 centimeters by 3 centimeters by 5 centimeters.
Unfold the prism into its net: two 4 by 3 ends, two 4 by 5 sides, two 3 by 5 sides.
The two ends together are 2 times 4 times 3, which is 24.
The two 4 by 5 sides together are 2 times 4 times 5, which is 40.
The two 3 by 5 sides together are 2 times 3 times 5, which is 30.
Add all three pairs: 24 + 40 + 30 = 94.
ways.example: A rectangular prism is 4 by 3 by 5 centimeters. Find its surface area.
ways.trap: Counting only one of each pair of matching faces instead of both.

figure.alt: A rectangular prism 4 by 3 by 5 centimeters, and its three pairs of matching faces.

frames.caption: Unfold into its net: three face pairs

ways.name: Wrap and cap
ways.when: Use this for a prism or cylinder: unroll the curved or side surface, then add the flat ends.
steps: A cylinder has radius 4 centimeters and height 6 centimeters.
Unroll the curved side into a rectangle: its width is the circumference, 2 pi times 4, or 8 pi, and its height is 6.
The lateral area is 8 pi times 6, which is 48 pi.
Each circular base has area pi times 4 squared, which is 16 pi; two bases give 32 pi.
Add the lateral area and the two bases: 48 pi + 32 pi = 80 pi.
ways.example: A cylinder has radius 4 centimeters and height 6 centimeters. Find its surface area, as a multiple of pi.
ways.trap: Adding only one base instead of both the top and bottom circle.

figure.alt: A cylinder, radius 4 and height 6 centimeters.

frames.caption: Unroll the curved side into a rectangle

ways.name: The formula table
ways.when: Use this once you can name the solid and recall its own surface area formula.
steps: A sphere has radius 6 centimeters.
A sphere's surface area formula is 4 times pi times its radius squared.
Square the radius: 6 times 6 is 36.
Multiply by 4: 4 times 36 is 144.
ways.example: A sphere has radius 6 centimeters. Find its surface area, as a multiple of pi.
ways.trap: Forgetting the factor of 4 and using just pi times radius squared.

figure.alt: A sphere of radius 6 centimeters, shown as a circle.

ways.name: Composite solids
ways.when: Use this when two solids are joined: add the outside faces, skip the ones hidden inside.
steps: A cylinder of radius 3 and height 10 centimeters is topped by a dome of the same radius.
The cylinder's lateral side is exposed: 2 times pi times 3 times 10, which is 60 pi.
The cylinder's bottom circle is exposed too: pi times 3 squared, which is 9 pi.
The cylinder's top circle is hidden under the dome, so skip it.
The dome's curved surface, half a sphere's surface, is 2 times pi times 3 squared, which is 18 pi.
Add the exposed pieces: 60 pi + 9 pi + 18 pi = 87 pi.
ways.example: A cylinder of radius 3 and height 10 centimeters is topped by a dome of the same radius. Find the exposed surface area, as a multiple of pi.
ways.trap: Adding every face of both solids, including the two hidden circles where they join.

figure.alt: A cylinder radius 3 height 10 centimeters, topped by a dome, with the hidden joint marked.

frames.caption: Top circle is hidden, skip it
